title: HDF Change Event Primitives
description: Shared building blocks for HDF change-event wire documents. The envelope is entity-agnostic: hdf-requirement-change-event composes it today, and any future sibling event type (e.g. component change events — hdf-comparison already models componentDiffs alongside requirementDiffs) reuses it verbatim.

eventId.description: Identity of this event occurrence, unique per source. (source, eventId) is the deduplication key: consumers may treat events with identical source and eventId as duplicates. UUIDv7 (time-ordered) is recommended but not required.

source.description: URI identifying the producer context that emitted this event (for example, a scanner instance and profile). eventId uniqueness and sequence numbering are scoped per source.

sequence.description: Monotonically increasing sequence number per entity key. The ONLY ordering authority for folding: consumers keep the greatest sequence per key regardless of arrival order or timestamp. Deliberately per-entity-key (event-sourcing aggregate-version practice) rather than per-source.

systemRef.description: URI to the hdf-system document (authorization boundary) this event applies to. Resolves to the latest version of the evolving system document.

componentId.description: componentId of the system component this event concerns.

timestamp.description: Occurrence time of the observed change (RFC 3339, trimmed UTC). Display and audit metadata only — NEVER an ordering key; ordering is sequence's job.

schemaRef.description: The versioned schema $id this event validates against, so events self-describe on heterogeneous streams. Recommended on every wire event.

priorChecksum.description: The effectiveChecksum of the entity state this event supersedes, forming a per-key hash chain: a mismatch or gap against stored state is detectable, letting a consumer mark the key unverified instead of serving stale posture. Null at chain start (no prior state, e.g. a new entity or the first event after a seed). The chain provides tamper/gap evidence given a trusted head; completeness is anchored out-of-band by periodic re-centering rescans.

examples.$comment: Steady-state envelope: mid-chain event from an InSpec producer. priorChecksum links to the previous effectiveChecksum for this key.
Chain-start envelope: first event for a key after seeding — priorChecksum is null (the CloudTrail null-previous-digest convention), sequence starts low.

Change_Event_Envelope.description: Entity-agnostic transport identity for a change event: dedup ((source, eventId)), ordering (per-key sequence), system anchor (systemRef + componentId), occurrence time, schema self-description, and the prior-state hash-chain link. Composed into each concrete event type via allOf; entity-specific keys and payload live on the event type.
Change_Event_Envelope.title: Change Event Envelope

Event_Requirement_State.description: The producer-computable subset of the comparison vocabulary's Requirement_State. Kept value-identical with the parent enum (test-enforced): the batch-only states (moved, split, merged) are outputs of cross-document identity resolution a per-key producer cannot compute. Declared as a distinct named type (rather than a $ref intersection) so generated Go/TS types keep stable, distinct enum names.
Event_Requirement_State.title: Event Requirement State

Event_Change_Reason.description: The producer-computable subset of the comparison vocabulary's Change_Reason, value-identical with the parent enum (test-enforced). Batch-only reasons (baselineUpgraded, controlMapped, scannerChanged, targetChanged, metadataChanged) require cross-corpus context and are excluded.
Event_Change_Reason.title: Event Change Reason

effectiveStatus.description: The resolved effective compliance status at this point in the chain.

effectiveImpact.description: The resolved effective impact score (0.0–1.0) at this point in the chain.

examples.$comment: Prior posture of a failing SSH-cipher control before remediation.
Prior posture of a control passing under a waiver (the projection carries the resolved status; the governing override type travels in the requirement payload, not here).

Effective_Projection.description: The minimal resolved-posture projection — the same field set the per-requirement effectiveChecksum hashes (status and impact; the governing disposition is carried by the full requirement payload).
Effective_Projection.title: Effective Projection

uri.description: URI to the seed snapshot document (relative path or absolute URL).

checksum.description: Checksum of the seed snapshot, REQUIRED: the derivation pins an immutable snapshot by content, not just location.

seed.$comment: Location + expected-hash reference (the SRI/OCI/SPDX pattern). Shares its core shape with hdf-evidence-package's Content_Reference and ADR-0006's proposed External_Reference; consolidation onto one reference primitive is tracked by bead hdf-libs-avp2.
seed.description: The authoritative snapshot this document was reassembled from, pinned by content.

source.description: URI of the event-stream producer context whose events were applied (matches the events' envelope source).

throughSequence.description: The event watermark: the highest per-key sequence number applied. Downstream precedence rule: a full-scan document supersedes the reconciled view as of its scan time; between scans, the reconciled document with the highest throughSequence is the current posture.

eventsApplied.description: Number of change events applied to the seed to produce this document.

asOf.description: The posture-as-of time of this reconciled view (RFC 3339, trimmed UTC) — the analog of PROV's generatedAtTime.

examples.$comment: A reconciled result set: reassembled from the pinned seed scan plus 3 change events through watermark 414. The document's generator names the reconciler, never the scanner.

Derivation.description: Derived-document lineage for a reconciled result set (an hdf-results produced by applyChangeEvents rather than a scanner). Records exactly which seed and event horizon the document represents so it can never masquerade as primary scan evidence. Conceptually PROV qualified derivation: derived entity, used entity (seed), activity (event application), generation time (asOf).
Derivation.title: Derivation
